$comment: The fleet's organisation, owned by humans (bin/guard.sh closes it to agent sessions). Every agent belongs to one family with a narrow purpose, a human owner accountable for its output, and a rung on the autonomy ladder. bin/admit.sh refuses a candidate this file does not name; bin/fleet-check.sh verifies FLEET.md agrees with it. OWNERS ARE A PLACEHOLDER: the suite ships capability, not accountability, so /forge:install asks who owns each family and writes the answers here.

ladder.assist: drafts for a human who accepts or amends; never commits scope
ladder.propose: commits on a ticket branch and proposes via pull request; a human merges
ladder.act: acts within deterministic gates; a human reviews the record

architecture.checkpoint: accepts the Contract inside the spec; boundary review of the plan by policy

qa.checkpoint: accepts the failing tests, which then lock (bin/accept.sh tests)

engineering.checkpoint: the gates; the independent reviewer's verdict

security.checkpoint: the reviewer's risk floor and the static analysis; no agent yet

intent-drafter.purpose: turn an issue into work/<T>/intent.md with open questions for the product owner to accept

spec-drafter.purpose: turn an accepted intent into work/<T>/spec.md: behaviour, acceptance criteria, a draft Contract, open questions

architect.purpose: correct the Contract and write ADRs before acceptance; boundary-review the plan and commit plan: after the lock

test-designer.purpose: draft failing tests from the accepted spec and prove them red for the QA lead to accept

implementer.purpose: draft plan.md, then make the locked tests pass with the smallest diff that keeps the gate green; commit impl:

release-manager.purpose: run both gate tiers, assemble evidence.json, commit evidence:, stop before the release
